Restore

/ri-STOR/ — stress on STOR · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To restore something is to repair it and bring it back to its original, good condition.

It took the museum three years to restore the ancient mosaic, tile by tile.

Worked Example

After the flood, the homeowners spent months restoring the Victorian cottage, carefully replacing rotted floorboards and repainting the walls in the original cream color.

Restore = re (again) + staurare (Latin: to set up) = to set it up again. The word means the homeowners are not just fixing damage — they're returning the cottage to its original good condition. That specificity makes restore far more precise than the plain word repair.

How Restore Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

repair

repair: fix something broken or damaged

renovate

rehabilitate

rehabilitate: bring back to health or usefulness

Antonyms

damage

damage: harm something so it no longer works well

ruin

ruin: destroy something beyond repair or usefulness

How Strong Is It? — patch → fix → repair → restore

patch vs. restore

patch vs. restore: You might patch a leaky roof to get through one storm, but to restore the whole house is to return it to its original glory.

fix vs. restore

fix vs. restore: Fixing a wobbly chair leg takes ten minutes, while restoring an antique chair to its original condition can take months of careful work.

repair vs. restore

repair vs. restore: A mechanic can repair the engine so it runs, but only a specialist can fully restore a classic car to gleaming showroom condition.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — re-

Prefix — re-: again (Latin)

Root — staurare

Root — staurare: to set up, make firm (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Re- (again) + staurare (to set up) literally means 'to set something up again' — to bring a thing back to the good, solid condition it once had.

Use the root in a new word: restaurant

Use the root in a new word: restaurant: A restaurant was originally named as a place that 'restored' weary travelers — after the long hike, we stopped at a small restaurant to refuel.

Word Building

Word Choice

neutral

Reach for restore when something broken or neglected is being fixed AND returned to its original good condition. For routine repairs, repair is simpler. For updates that improve beyond the original, renovate is clearer.
